prompt: Which of these is one of the three things `app.use(router)` does in the planner?
hint: The section lists them right after `main.js`.

choices.text: Builds the routes from the folders under `src/pages`
choices.why: That is version 5's routing by file, which this lesson does not use; the planner writes its routes by hand in `router.js`.

choices.text: Calls `createRouter` with the list in `router.js`
choices.why: It is the other way round: `createRouter` has already run, at the import, and `app.use` installs what it made.

choices.text: Registers `<RouterView>` and `<RouterLink>`
choices.why: Right. Together with providing the router and starting to listen to the address bar.

choices.text: Reloads the page whenever the address changes
choices.why: Changing the screen without a reload is the whole point of a router.

prompt: `npm install --save-___ vue-router@5.4.0` writes `"5.4.0"` into `package.json` with no caret.
hint: The flag that pins a version.

prompt: In the planner, where is the view that matches the address drawn?
hint: Look at `App.vue`'s template.

choices.text: In place of `App`, which the router takes off the page
choices.why: `App` stays: its header and footer are drawn on every page, around the view.

choices.text: Inside the `<RouterLink>` that was clicked
choices.why: A link only asks the router to change the screen; it draws an `<a>` and nothing else.

choices.text: Beside `App`, in the `#app` element of `index.html`
choices.why: `#app` holds `App` alone; the view is inside it, one level down.

choices.text: In `App`'s `<RouterView />`, inside `<main>`
choices.why: Right. Between the header and the footer, which stay on every page.

prompt: Why does `CourseCard` link with `<RouterLink>` rather than a plain `<a href>`?
hint: What happens to the application's refs on each kind of click?

choices.text: A plain `<a>` would reload the whole application on each click
choices.why: Right. And loses every ref that was not saved; `<RouterLink>` stops the load and asks the router instead.

choices.text: A plain `<a>` to `/courses/spanish` gets a 404 from the dev server
choices.why: The dev server answers every such address with `index.html`; the history section shows it.

choices.text: `<RouterLink>` is the one a reader can open in a new tab
choices.why: Both are an `<a href>` in the page, so both open in a new tab and read as a link.

choices.text: The router ignores an address it did not change itself
choices.why: The router reads the address bar on start and on back and forward too, whoever wrote it.

prompt: Which of these are true of the planner's `router.js`? Choose all that apply.
hint: Read the notes beside each part of the example.

choices.text: `name` lets a link refer to a route without spelling its path
choices.why: Right. `CourseView`'s links use `course-week` and `course-all`.

choices.text: `HomeView` is loaded lazily, like the course's views
choices.why: It is imported at the top, normally: the week is the page everybody sees first.

choices.text: `meta.title` is read by `afterEach`
choices.why: Right. `meta` is free-form, and the planner's `afterEach` builds the tab's title from it.

choices.text: `createWebHistory` writes each address after a `#`
choices.why: That is `createWebHashHistory`; `createWebHistory` gives real paths such as `/courses/spanish`.

prompt: The route `/courses/:id` says `props: true`. How does `CourseView` learn which course to show?
hint: Look at the first lines of its `<script setup>`.

choices.text: It parses `window.location.pathname` in setup
choices.why: Nothing in the view reads the address; the router has already matched it.

choices.text: `App` passes `id` to its `<RouterView>`
choices.why: `App`'s `<RouterView />` has no attributes; the `:course="id"` is on the one inside `CourseView`, for its children.

choices.text: `defineProps` declares `id`, which the router fills from `params.id`
choices.why: Right. `props: true` hands every parameter over as a prop of the same name.

choices.text: It calls `useRoute()`, and `props: true` makes that result reactive
choices.why: `useRoute()` is reactive with or without `props: true`, and `CourseView` does not call it.

prompt: A view of `/courses/:id` copies its course's data into a ref once, in setup, from its `id` prop. The student follows a link from `/courses/spanish` to `/courses/guitar`. What does the view show?
hint: Does the router make a new component for the new address?

choices.text: The new course, because each address gets a component of its own
choices.why: The route is the same, so the router reuses the component and only changes the prop.

choices.text: The first course's data, under the new address
choices.why: Right. Setup ran once, with `spanish`; only a `computed` or a watcher of `id` would follow the change.

choices.text: Nothing, while the router destroys the old view and builds a new one
choices.why: There is no destroying: reusing the component is what makes the switch fast.

choices.text: The not-found page, since setup does not run for the new `id`
choices.why: Setup not running again is true, and it leaves the old data on screen; nothing sends the student elsewhere.

prompt: Why does the lesson prefer the `id` prop to `useRoute().params.id`?
hint: Think about lesson 21, and what each view needs around it.

choices.text: `useRoute()` is not reactive, so it misses a new parameter
choices.why: The route `useRoute()` returns is reactive; the preference is about what the view depends on.

choices.text: A prop works with no router around it
choices.why: Right. Giving the view an `id` is enough to use and test it; `useRoute()` needs a whole router.

choices.text: A prop is quicker, because the router skips resolving the route
choices.why: The route is resolved the same way either way; `props: true` only changes how the view receives it.

choices.text: `useRoute()` works in the matched view and not in its children
choices.why: It works in any component under the router; `NotFound` and any child could call it.

prompt: On `/courses/spanish/all`, the captured HTML of the Sessions nav has two links. How many of them carry the class `router-link-active`?
hint: Read each `class` attribute in the capture.

prompt: On `/courses/spanish/all`, what is on the All sessions link in the captured HTML? Choose all that apply.
hint: Some of the attributes come from the router and one from the scoped style.

choices.text: `aria-current="page"`
choices.why: Right. The router sets it on the exact link, so a screen reader announces the current page.

choices.text: `aria-selected="true"`, written by the router for the screen reader
choices.why: The router's attribute for this is `aria-current`; `aria-selected` belongs to tabs and options.

choices.text: The class `router-link-exact-active`
choices.why: Right. Its route is exactly the current one, and `CourseView`'s style makes it bold.

choices.text: The class `router-link-active`
choices.why: Right. An exact link is also an active one, so it carries both classes.

choices.text: `data-v-62175599`, the router's mark for the active link
choices.why: That attribute is on both links and on the nav: it is the scoped style's, from the compiler.

prompt: A settings page keeps a list of five categories on screen, and the form beside it changes with `/settings/profile`, `/settings/billing` and so on. How would this lesson route it?
hint: Which part of the screen stays, and which part changes with the address?

choices.text: Five top-level routes, as nesting is for paths that look nested
choices.why: The lesson's test is the screen, not the path: here part of the page stays, which is the case for nesting.

choices.text: One route, with the form switched by a ref
choices.why: Then `/settings/billing` could not be bookmarked or reached with back: the address would not change.

choices.text: A parent drawing the list and a `<RouterView>`, with a child route per category
choices.why: Right. The list is the part that stays, the form is the part that changes, as in the course page.

choices.text: A child route per category, each drawing the list of categories again
choices.why: A child is drawn inside the parent's `<RouterView>`, so the list belongs in the parent, drawn once.

prompt: In the planner as written, the student is on `/courses/spanish` and follows a link to `/courses/latin`. What happens?
hint: Which guard runs when only a parameter changes?

choices.text: `beforeEnter` runs and redirects to the not-found page
choices.why: That is what a fresh entry does; going from one course to another by a link only changes `:id`.

choices.text: No guard checks it, and a course page headed `latin` is drawn
choices.why: Right. `beforeEnter` runs on entering the route, not when only its params change.

choices.text: The router reloads the page, and then `beforeEnter` runs
choices.why: A link never reloads; a reload is what would make it a fresh entry.

choices.text: `afterEach` sees the unknown course and cancels
choices.why: The planner's `afterEach` only sets the title, and by then the navigation has already happened.

prompt: Why does the course route's guard fetch `courses.json` itself instead of using `App`'s data?
hint: Where does a guard run?

choices.text: Guards have to be synchronous, so they cannot wait for `inject`
choices.why: A guard can be `async`, and the router waits for it; this one awaits a fetch.

choices.text: It runs outside any component, so `App`'s provide is out of reach
choices.why: Right. The duplicated load is the cue for lesson 13's store, a module a guard can import.

choices.text: Injected data is a copy taken at start-up
choices.why: `inject` hands over the same refs `App` holds, not a copy; the guard simply cannot reach them.

choices.text: A fetch inside a guard is faster than reading a ref
choices.why: It is slower, a second request; it is there because there is no other way yet.

prompt: Which of these, returned by a guard, let the navigation go ahead to where it was heading? Choose all that apply.
hint: A location goes somewhere; one value stays put.

choices.text: `false`
choices.why: `false` cancels it and leaves the student where they were.

choices.text: Nothing at all, `undefined`
choices.why: Right. A guard that returns nothing lets the navigation continue.

choices.text: A location such as `{ name: 'home' }`
choices.why: A location redirects: the navigation goes there instead.

choices.text: `true`
choices.why: Right. The same as returning nothing.

prompt: The planner sets `document.title` in `router.___((to) => …)`, the hook the router calls once a navigation is over.
hint: It is the last guard in the lesson's table but one.

prompt: How does `router.js` make `CourseView` load lazily?
hint: Look at the course route's `component`.

choices.text: `component: CourseView, lazy: true` on the route
choices.why: There is no `lazy` option; the laziness is in giving a function instead of the component.

choices.text: `component: () => import('./views/CourseView.vue')`
choices.why: Right. The function runs the first time the route is opened, and the import becomes a file of its own.

choices.text: An `import` of it at the top of the file
choices.why: That is how `HomeView` and `NotFound` are imported, eagerly, into the first file.

choices.text: `props: true`, which defers the view until a parameter arrives
choices.why: `props: true` only passes the parameters as props; it has nothing to do with loading.

prompt: In the output of `npm run build`, how many `.js` files in `dist/assets` came from lazily imported views?
hint: Count the `.js` lines other than `index-….js`.

prompt: `NotFound` is small and rarely seen. Why is it imported eagerly all the same?
hint: When is that page shown?

choices.text: A route whose path is `(.*)*` refuses a lazy component
choices.why: Any route can take a lazy component; keeping this one eager was a choice.

choices.text: Vite does not split off a file smaller than 2 kB
choices.why: Vite split off `CourseAll` at 0.50 kB; the 2 kB in the lesson is about what a request costs.

choices.text: It appears when something is already wrong, so one more request must not be needed
choices.why: Right. That is not the moment to depend on one more request succeeding.

choices.text: `beforeEnter` redirects to it before lazy files are allowed to load
choices.why: Lazy files load during a navigation, redirected or not; the course views load after the guard in the capture.

prompt: After the click on Spanish, the dev server's network list shows four requests. Which one was made by the course route's guard rather than by lazy loading?
hint: What does `courseExists` ask for?

choices.text: `GET /src/views/CourseWeek.vue`
choices.why: That is the child view, imported lazily by the `''` child route.

choices.text: `GET /src/views/CourseView.vue?vue&type=style…`
choices.why: That is `CourseView`'s scoped style, which arrives with the lazily loaded component.

choices.text: `GET /courses.json`
choices.why: Right. `courseExists` fetches the data file again, before the views are loaded.

choices.text: `GET /src/views/CourseView.vue`
choices.why: That is the course page itself, the lazy import in the course route's `component`.

prompt: The built planner is served from `dist` with `python3 -m http.server`. Which of these gets a 404?
hint: Which requests reach the server, and for which path?

choices.text: Clicking a course card after opening `/`
choices.why: A click asks nothing of the server for the page: the router changes the address and draws the course.

choices.text: Reloading the page while on `/courses/spanish`
choices.why: Right. The browser asks for that path, and `dist` has no file called `courses/spanish`.

choices.text: Opening `/` for the first time on a new computer
choices.why: `/` is `index.html`, a file that exists, and the capture shows it answering 200.

choices.text: The browser fetching `assets/index-….js` from the built `index.html`
choices.why: That file is in `dist/assets`, so a plain server finds it.

prompt: Which of these make a reload of `/courses/spanish` draw the course? Choose all that apply.
hint: Either the server falls back, or the path never reaches it.

choices.text: Setting the host to answer any path that is not a file with `index.html`
choices.why: Right. That is the fallback, under names such as rewrites or SPA mode.

choices.text: Importing `CourseView` eagerly
choices.why: The 404 comes from the server before any of the application's code runs, eager or lazy.

choices.text: Serving the build with `npm run preview`
choices.why: Right. Vite's preview server falls back to `index.html`.

choices.text: Switching the router to `createWebHashHistory()`
choices.why: Right. The address becomes `/#/courses/spanish`, and what follows `#` is not sent.

choices.text: Adding a `beforeEnter` guard to the course route
choices.why: A guard runs inside the application, and the application never starts when the server answers 404.

prompt: Why does `createWebHashHistory()` need no server configuration?
hint: What does the browser send when it asks for `/#/courses/spanish`?

choices.text: Hash addresses are kept in the browser's cache after the first visit
choices.why: Caching is not involved; even a first visit to a hash address works.

choices.text: The router answers the request before the server sees it
choices.why: The router is code in the page, so it cannot run before the page has arrived.

choices.text: Servers drop the path of any request that contains `#`
choices.why: The server never receives a `#`; the browser leaves it out of the request.

choices.text: The part after `#` is never sent, so every reload asks for `/`
choices.why: Right. The cost is the `#` in every address.

pairs.right: check that a parameter names something real

right_distractors: react when only the parameter changes

prompt: A student bookmarks `/courses/guitar/all` and opens it next week, on the built planner served by a plain static server. What do they see?
hint: Who answers first: the server or the router?

choices.text: A bare 404 page, and no sign of the application
choices.why: Right. There is no such file in `dist`, so the application, and its router, never start.

choices.text: The not-found page, drawn by the `(.*)*` route
choices.why: That route is the router's, and the router is in `index.html`'s scripts, which the server did not send.

choices.text: Guitar's sessions, since the address names a real route
choices.why: It names a real route of the application, but the server has to send the application first.

choices.text: The week, because the router falls back to `/` for a bookmark
choices.why: No part of the router falls back to `/`; the fallback in the lesson is the server's, and this one has none.
